'''''Sternbergia lutea''''', the '''winter daffodil''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=STLU4|taxon=Sternbergia lutea|accessdate=3 December 2015}}</ref><ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> '''autumn daffodil''', '''fall daffodil''', '''lily-of-the-field''', or '''yellow autumn crocus''',{{efn|Though it does not belong to the same family as the [[crocus]].}} is a [[bulb]]ous [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Amaryllidaceae]], subfamily [[Amaryllidoideae]],<ref>{{citation |last=Stevens |first=P.F.  |title=Angiosperm Phylogeny Website: Asparagales: Amaryllidoideae |url=http://www.mobot.org/mobot/research/apweb/orders/asparagalesweb.htm#AllAma }}</ref> in the [[Narcisseae]] tribe, which is used as an [[ornamental plant]]. It has yellow flowers which appear in autumn.

The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''lutea'' means "yellow".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book | last=Harrison |first=Lorraine | title=RHS Latin for Gardeners | year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley | location=United Kingdom | isbn=978-1845337315 }}</ref>

==Description==

[[Image:Sternbergia lutea showing the different parts of the flower.JPG|thumb|center|The six grey-striated tepals, the six yellow stamens, and the style with its stigma]]

''Sternbergia lutea'' has a wide distribution from the [[Balearic Islands]] in the Western Mediterranean through to [[Tajikistan]] in Central Asia.<ref name=Kew1>{{Citation |author=WCSP |year=2011 |title=World Checklist of Selected Plant Families |publisher=The Board of Trustees of the [[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] |url=http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/ |access-date=2011-09-20 }}, search for "Sternbergia lutea"</ref> It dies down to a bulb during the summer. Leaves first appear in the autumn (September to November in its native habitats), and are glossy green, up to 12 mm wide; they remain through the winter.

Deep yellow flowers appear soon after the leaves, with six [[tepal]]s around 3–3.5 cm long,<ref name=Mathew1987>{{Citation |last=Mathew |first=Brian |year=1987 |title=The Smaller Bulbs |publication-place=London |publisher=B.T. Batsford |isbn=978-0-7134-4922-8 }}, p. 157–159</ref> six yellow stamens and a style with a single stigma.

Smaller forms with narrower leaves (up to 5 mm wide) and narrower tepals (3–12 mm rather than 10–20 mm) have been separated off under various names (e.g. ''S. lutea'' var. ''graeca'', ''S. sicula'').<ref name=Mathew1987/>

==Subspecies==
Three subspecies are accepted.<ref name = powo>[https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:60471738-2 ''Sternbergia lutea'' (L.) Ker Gawl. ex Spreng.] ''[[Plants of the World Online]]''. Retrieved 24 August 2024.</ref>
*''Sternbergia lutea'' subsp. ''greuteriana'' {{small|(Kamari & R.Artelari) Strid}} (synonyms ''Sternbergia greuteriana'' {{small|Kamari & R.Artelari}} and ''S. minoica'' {{small|Ravenna}}) – Crete
*''Sternbergia lutea'' subsp. ''lutea'' (synonyms ''Sternbergia angustifolia'' {{small|Krelage}} and ''S. aurantiaca'' {{small|Dinsm}}) – southern Europe to western Asia, the Caucasus, and Tajikistan
*''Sternbergia lutea'' subsp. ''sicula'' {{small|(Tineo ex Guss.) K.Richt.}} (synonyms ''Oporanthus siculus'' {{small|(Tineo ex Guss.) Parl.}} and ''S. sicula'' {{small|Tineo ex Guss.}}) – Italy, Sicily, Greece, Crete, and western Turkey

== Cultivation ==
''Sternbergia lutea'' is hardy to [[Hardiness zone|USDA hardiness zones]] 7–9 (−18 to −1 °C) depending on the degree of protection given.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Evans |first1=Erv |last2=De Hertough |first2=A.A. |title=Sternbergia lutea; Winter daffodil, Fall daffodil, Yellow Autumn crocus |publisher=NC State University |url=http://www.ces.ncsu.edu/depts/hort/consumer/factsheets/bulbs-summer/sternbergia.html |access-date=2011-09-20 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927003109/http://www.ces.ncsu.edu/depts/hort/consumer/factsheets/bulbs-summer/sternbergia.html |archivedate=2011-09-27 |url-status=dead |name-list-style=amp }}</ref> It can be grown outside in the [[British Isles]] in well-drained soil; a warm dry period in summer is required for good flowering. Alkaline soils are recommended. Bulbs are usually planted while dormant (i.e. in late summer or early autumn), but can be lifted and divided before the leaves die down in late spring.<ref name=Mathew1987/>

This plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web 
| url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/17789/i-Sternbergia-lutea-i/Details
| title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Sternbergia lutea'' | access-date = 21 November 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web 
| url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 
| page = 99 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 21 November 2018}}</ref>

A vigorous form with narrow leaves is grown in gardens under the name ''S. lutea'' var. ''angustifolia''.<ref name=Mathew1987/>
